data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Idempotence and safety are not competing properties but complementary requirements at different system boundaries. Idempotence at the consumer/processing layer implies safety at the storage/log layer. The append-only event log requires safety of its writers (the log tolerates duplicates without corruption of its structure), and this safety is in turn achieved by requiring idempotence of its readers (processing the same event twice yields the same state). The log does not demand writer idempotence \u2014 it demands writer safety, which is a strictly weaker condition.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log and consumer are tightly coupled (e.g., in-process event sourcing with no separate deduplication layer), the two-boundary model collapses and the log alone must provide both safety and some form of idempotence guarantee.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If consumers are non-idempotent by design (e.g., events represent increments to a counter without deduplication), safety at the log level cannot rescue deterministic replay.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log supports causal ordering or dependency tracking that is broken by duplicate entries (e.g., duplicate entries create false causal dependencies), then safety at the structural level may not be sufficient.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Two-boundary model: (1) Writer\u2192Log boundary: the write operation must be safe \u2014 appending a duplicate entry does not violate the log's structural invariants (append-only, monotonically ordered, internally consistent). This is trivially satisfied by append-only semantics. (2) Log\u2192Consumer boundary: the read-and-process operation must be idempotent \u2014 reprocessing a previously seen event produces no additional state change. This is achieved through consumer-side deduplication (event IDs, sequence numbers, or content hashing). The composition of safe writes and idempotent reads yields deterministic replay under at-least-once delivery: the replayed log (with duplicates) produces the same final state as the original processing because each duplicate is safely stored and idempotently consumed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
